objective.value: Given free-text U.S. start and finish locations, return a driving route, ordered fuel stops chosen for lowest reachable $/gal within a 500-mile tank, and total fuel cost at 10 MPG with an auditable per-stop breakdown.

repositoryNote.value: Public repository with API contract (API_CONTRACT.md), OpenAPI/Swagger docs, and optional React + Leaflet UI.

measuredOutcomes.value: Repository design budget: cold request ≤ 3 external HTTP calls (2 geocode + 1 route); warm/cached often 0; per-station network calls always 0 (coordinates attached at ingest).

problem.value: Plan a U.S. driving route while choosing fuel stops for lowest reachable price per gallon within tank range, with auditable cost totals — not an opaque black-box recommendation.

overview.value: API-first logistics planner: Django REST backend geocodes endpoints (Nominatim), fetches drive geometry (OSRM), selects cheapest reachable corridor stops from an ingested fuel-price dataset, and returns polyline, ordered stops, and totals. Optional React + Leaflet UI for demos.

architecture.value: Client POST /api/v1/route/ { start, finish } → geocode (Nominatim, cached) → drive route (OSRM, cached) → load corridor stations from DB → pick cheapest reachable stop each tank window → return geometry + stops + totals + meta.external_calls. Vehicle constants: MAX_RANGE_MILES = 500, MPG = 10.

decisions.value: API-first with an optional React UI: core value is the route/fuel planning contract (documented OpenAPI and API_CONTRACT.md), with the map UI treated as a demo surface rather than the source of truth.

tradeoffs.value: External-call budget versus freshness: geocode and route results are cached so warm requests avoid repeat Nominatim/OSRM calls; station prices are loaded from the ingested CSV into SQLite so planning never issues per-station network calls.

constraints.value: Tank range fixed at 500 miles and fuel economy at 10 MPG (named constants). Free Nominatim and public OSRM demo endpoints; fuel prices from the assessment CSV loaded once into SQLite.
